We need the template that matches SN2: break C-Cl (alkyl halide) and form C-N (primary/secondary amine). Look through results: The first result is not SN2. Second result: retro_smarts_template '[C:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]...>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]...' This seems like conversion of alkyl chain to carbonyl? Not SN2.

Third result: retro_smarts_template '[C:2]-[NH;D2;+0:1]-[c:3]>>O=C(-O-C-c1...)-[N;H0;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[c:3]' Not SN2.

Fourth result: looks like SN2? retro_smarts_template '[C:6]-[NH;D2;+0:7]-[c;H0;D3;+0:2]...>>C-C(-C)-N(-C-[CH3;D1;+0:1])-C(-C)-C.Cl-...' This seems to involve a chloride attached to aromatic? Might be SN2.

But we need a template that can be applied to our target molecule. The target has a benzylic carbon attached to N4CC(F)C4 via a CH2 (C N). The leaving group maybe a chloride originally attached to that benzylic carbon. So template should have pattern: [C:1]-[Cl]>>[C:1]-[N] (primary/secondary amine). Look for template where retro_smarts includes [C:...]-Cl and product includes [C:...]-[N]. In results, I see none obvious. Maybe need to search with bonds_broken ["C-Cl"] and bonds_formed ["C-N"].

Let's try search with bonds_broken ["C-Cl"] and bonds_formed ["C-N"].
